author: blu
body: The Real family did not, and the asymmetry was invisible for as long as nobody wrote `unit Real`: passing a `Metre` where a `Real` was expected raised CDX2001 while the identical Integer program compiled. Half a feature, and the half that was missing is the one a shader wants, since every physical quantity in one is a Real.

author: reek
body: scope-grants holds the effect labels the def under check declares, so an operation deep in the body can be measured against the scope its signature granted. It is per-def context, set once at the def boundary like effect-exempt, never threaded through unification.

author: reek
body: chapter-grounds is different: it is per-COMPILE context, the whole chapter's grounds table ("slug\neffect" entries) set once when checking begins and constant across every def. check-def-normal looks up the def's own chapter-slug in it to find which hardware effects that chapter is the source of, and admits exactly those in the def's body without a declaration.

author: reek
body: Rows solve against their own table (see State above). make-row is the canonical constructor: labels sorted by name then scope, duplicate-free, so structural equality is set equality and the merge in unify-row is a single linear walk. Rows in practice carry at most a couple of labels; nothing here recurses into types.

author: reek
body: A slot is unbound while it still holds its self-row. The occurs check forbids binding row id i to a row whose tail chain reaches i, so a stored binding can never look like the self-row.

author: reek
body: Binding grows the table with self-row fillers up to the bound id, so fresh ids alone allocate nothing and the table stays index-dense.

author: reek
body: The row occurs check is a walk of the tail substitution chain -- rows do not nest, so there is no recursion into types. Binding a tail to a row whose resolved chain reaches that same tail would create an infinite row.

author: reek
body: Closed against closed (and same-tail against same-tail: a tail cannot absorb labels on one side of itself) requires the label sets to already agree.

author: reek
body: Open against closed: the closed side cannot absorb the open side's extra labels, so those must be empty; the open tail then absorbs exactly the closed side's leftovers and closes. The binding target is a closed row, so no occurs check is needed on this path.

author: reek
body: Open against open with distinct tails: each tail absorbs the other side's leftovers, sharing one fresh remainder. Both binding targets end in the fresh tail, so a cycle is impossible by construction -- the occurs check stands as defense in depth.

author: reek
body: The EffectfulTy stripping arms are gone (stage 3b): an effectful VALUE type unifies structurally -- set-equal effect names and unifiable inner types -- and never silently sheds its effects against a bare type. Concrete effects on ARROWS live in the row and unify through unify-row inside unify-fun.

author: reek
body: A `unit` wrapper is transparent to its inner type at a boundary: the guide's example is passing a `Second` where an `Integer` is expected, and that has always worked because the `IntegerTy` arm below unwraps a `UnitTy` on the right. The `UnitTy` arm handles the mirror direction generically, so a unit on the LEFT unwraps against anything.

author: reek
body: Every Real takes the arm whatever its width and mode, not only the default one. Fixing the case with a failing example and leaving the others is how a defect grows a long tail.

author: reek
body: Same-named type constructors must be applied at the same arity. Unifying only the common prefix and silently succeeding on the extra arguments (either side) would let `Foo A B` unify with `Foo A`. The declared-type arity checker (CDX2050) catches this in signatures, so this is defense-in-depth for constructed types synthesized during inference: a length mismatch is a type mismatch, not a match on the overlap. The length is compared once at entry (len is the caller's list-length args-a); the loop then walks the equal-length lists.

author: reek
body: Most types reaching deep-resolve are already fully resolved -- the checker ran first and unified everything. Short-circuit when the input has no TypeVars: a single fold-only pass that allocates nothing and returns the original tree. Otherwise fall through to the full map-children rebuild.

author: reek
body: The snapshot must cover both substitution tables: a speculative unify inside a GADT arm can bind row tails as well as type variables, and a restore that rolled back only one table would leave the other holding bindings from the abandoned branch.
